headline: New Zealand Court Finds Pay-Equity Law Inconsistent With Sex-Discrimination Right
deck: Declaration leaves the amended law in force while the Crown retains an appeal route.
body: New Zealand’s High Court has made a formal declaration that the amended Equal Pay Act is inconsistent with the right to be free from discrimination on the basis of sex, including the right to be free from pay inequity. [E1]

The court found that the Act treated women in women-dominated workforces differently from employees who did not rely on it for that right, materially disadvantaging those women without demonstrable justification. [E2]

The declaration does not cancel the law, which remains in force, and the Crown can appeal. [E3] The amendments discontinued all current pay-equity claims and made review clauses in existing settlements unenforceable. [E4] New claims can be raised under the amended Act if they meet its requirements. [E5]
